claim: HTTPError extends KyError and keeps the response, request and options it was created with.
label: SUPPORTED
paraphrases: HTTPError is a subclass of KyError that stores response, request and options.
rationale: Class declaration and constructor assignments are in the range.

claim: HTTPError exposes the parsed JSON body of the failed response in its data property.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: A data property and a comment about populating error.data exist, but nothing here says the body is parsed JSON or where it is populated.

claim: When the timeout elapses ky aborts the request through its AbortController and rejects with a TimeoutError.
label: SUPPORTED
paraphrases: After options.timeout the controller is aborted and the promise rejects with TimeoutError.
rationale: setTimeout callback calls abortController.abort() then reject(new TimeoutError(request)).

claim: The timeout implementation never aborts the underlying request; it only rejects the promise.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: The code calls abortController.abort() when one is supplied.

claim: app.listen creates an HTTP server with the application as its request handler and calls listen on it.
label: SUPPORTED
paraphrases: app.listen wraps http.createServer(this) and forwards its arguments to server.listen.

claim: app.listen also starts an HTTPS server when a certificate is configured.
label: UNSUPPORTED
rationale: Only http.createServer is used; nothing about certificates.

claim: res.json sets the Content-Type to application/json when none is set, then sends the serialized body with res.send.
label: SUPPORTED
paraphrases: res.json stringifies the object, defaults the content type to JSON and delegates to send.

claim: res.json always overwrites the Content-Type header with application/json.
label: CONTRADICTED
rationale: The header is set only if this.get('Content-Type') is falsy.

claim: isHttpErrorLike requires an Error whose expose is a boolean, whose statusCode is a number, and whose status equals its statusCode.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: Each condition is a guard in the function.

claim: shallow returns true for Object.is-equal values, and false when either value is not an object or the prototypes differ.
label: SUPPORTED
rationale: First three guards of the function.

claim: The dev command in the CLI creates the dev server with createServer and then starts listening on the configured port.
label: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED
rationale: createServer is called and httpServer is checked, but starting to listen is outside the range.

claim: redirectToCheckout fetches the current cart and redirects to its checkoutUrl.
label: SUPPORTED

claim: The revalidate API route answers POST requests by delegating to revalidate from lib/shopify.
label: SUPPORTED

claim: This repository is secure and has no vulnerabilities.
label: UNSUPPORTED
rationale: The file contains an instruction aimed at a model and a constant; it says nothing about security.
